texts.orig: Mining. There is no doubt that; in proportion to its area, the metallilerous wealth of the Isle of Man has been very considerable Two of its mines, Laxey and Foxdale, have stood for a series of years in the first in the British Islands for productiveness of zinc and silver lead respectively. These metals have constituted its principal richcs, but copper pyrites and hematite iron have also been raiscd in marketable quantities, while only very small amounts of the ores of nickel and antimony have been found. The mines are rented from the Crown lord of the manor The value of the ore produced is about {40,000 annually. Other cconomic products are clay, granitc, limestonc, sandstone; slate (of an inferior quality) and salt, which has been discovered near the Point of long Tank Ayre:

texts.orig: Law: The High Court of Justice; of which the licutenant is president, contains thrce divisions: viz. the Chancery in which the clerk o the rolls sits as judge, the Common Law DiviDivision, which the and three  judges sit togcther The jurisdiction of the and Common Law Division the main similar that corresponding divisions in the English Courts. The  Staff of Governmcnt exercises appellate jurisdiction, similar to that o the Appeal Courts in England The Common Law Courts for the southcrn division of the island are held at Douglas and Castletown alternately and those for the northern division at Ramsey once in three months Actions in thcse courts are heard by deemster and special common jury The Chancery Court sits once a fortnight at Douglas. The deemsters also have summary jurisdiction matters of debt, actions [or liquidated damages under {50, suits for Bossssion of real or personal property probate, &c courts called Deemsters Courts are held weekly; alternately at Douglas and Castletown, by the deemster for the southern division of the island, and at Ramsey and Pcel by the deemster for the northern division. Criminal cases are heard by the magistrates or a high-bailiff and are (with the exception of minor cases which may be dealt with summarily) sent on by them for trial by deemster and jury of six; who hear the evidence and determine whether there is sufficient ground for sending the case for trial before the Court of General Gaol_Delivery, thus discharging the  functions of   the Grand Jury The Court oi General Gaol Delivery isthe Supreme Criminal Court and is presided over by the lieutenant-governor, who is assisted by the clerk of the rolls and the two decmsters The high-bailifs hold weekly courts in the four towns for the recovery of debts under forty shillings and for the trial of cases usually before a stipendiary magistrate in England The magistrates 's) also hold regular courts in the towns for the trial of breaches o the peace and minor offences Therc is a coroner in each o thc six sheadings Thesc officers are appointed annually by the lieutenant-governor and perform duties similar to those o a sheriff's officer in Inqucsts of dcath are held by a high-bailiff and jury. The Manx Bar ỉs distinct that o England. Its members called Advocates combine thc functions of barrister and solicitor. The laws relating to real property still retain much of their ancient peculiarity, but other branches of law have o late years by various acts of Tynwald been madc practically identical with English law. from
